recommendations.regimenLabel: IV saline rehydration + bisphosphonate (± calcitonin for rapid control)
steps: Aggressive IV 0.9% saline rehydration (cornerstone) with monitoring of fluid status.
IV bisphosphonate (e.g. zoledronic acid) for moderate-severe hypercalcaemia (effect over 2-4 days).
Calcitonin for rapid short-term lowering in severe/symptomatic cases.
Avoid thiazides; stop calcium/vitamin D; treat the underlying cause (malignancy, hyperparathyroidism).

drugRefs.dose: 3-4 L over 24 h (e.g. 200-300 mL/h, titrate to fluid status)
drugRefs.why: Cornerstone of treatment — restores volume and enhances urinary calcium excretion. Monitor for fluid overload in cardiac/renal patients.
Inhibits osteoclastic bone resorption for moderate-severe hypercalcaemia; onset over 2-4 days. Reduce/adjust in renal impairment.
Rapid but short-lived (tachyphylaxis) fall in calcium while the bisphosphonate takes effect, in severe/symptomatic cases.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Disorders of Calcium Metabolism

drugRefs.freq: as per malignancy protocol (e.g. weekly loading then monthly)
drugRefs.why: Option for malignant hypercalcaemia refractory to bisphosphonates, including in renal impairment where bisphosphonates are limited.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Disorders of Calcium Metabolism

decision.label: IV saline + IV bisphosphonate (± calcitonin if severe)

confirm: Confusion, polyuria, constipation, abdominal pain with raised corrected calcium; PTH distinguishes hyperparathyroidism from malignancy/other.
